correctness.rationale: The exact Ferroni base structure yields two vertex orbits under S_r x S_t. Uniqueness of minimum enclosing sphere and symmetry force center c(q) in affine hyperplane sum x=r. Squared orbit distances are d0²=(n/(rt))q², d1²=2+(n/(rt))q²-2(n/(rt))q. Their minimax has unique q*=min(1,rt/n). Contact-barycenter certificates c(q*)=(1-q*)v0+(q*/rt)sum exchanges in the first regime, c(1)=mean exchanges in the second, prove global minimality for every r,t positive. Exact independent rational checks covered 1,770 pairs 2<=n<=60, supporting but not replacing minimax proof. Boundaries r=1,t=1,(r,t)=(2,2) verified.
residual_risks: Only canonical indicator-vector realization with inherited Euclidean norm, not arbitrary affine images.
Finite numeric SciPy verify.py is corroborative; exact global proof is symbolic minimax and convex-hull certificate.

value.rationale: Minimal matroids form a distinguished extremal matroid family; their canonical base polytopes have a natural Euclidean circumball invariant. The exact discrete transition classifies which bases support the unique enclosing sphere and singles out the exceptional T_{2,4} equality, with an explicit rank/corank-stable center formula. Although short once the vertex structure is known, this is a useful exact metric classification, not an arbitrary slice or mere known-table computation.
residual_risks: No claim about Löwner/John ellipsoid or radius of general matroid polytopes.

final_claim: For T_{r,n} with n=r+t and rt+1 vertices A,(A-i)+j, the minimum Euclidean sphere transitions at rt=n: q*=min(1,rt/n), center (1-q*/r)1_A+(q*/t)1_B; all vertices contact for rt<=n and only rt exchanges contact for rt>n; radii squared respectively rt/n and 2-n/(rt).
limitations: The source is canonical Euclidean coordinates; affine transformations need not preserve radius.
Root-orbit second-phase theorem is partial prior coverage.
